title: Scientific Opinion on the substantiation of health claims related to live yoghurt cultures and improved lactose digestion (ID 1143, 2976) pursuant to Article 13(1) of Regulation (EC) No 1924/2006
authors: EFSA Panel on Dietetic Products, Nutrition and Allergies (NDA)
funder: European Food Safety Authority, on request from the European Commission (Questions EFSA-Q-2008-1882, EFSA-Q-2008-3708). The evidence assessed was supplied by Member States and stakeholders.
authorConflicts: One panel member did not take part in the discussion because of potential conflicts of interest.
result: Thirteen of 14 human studies showed enhanced digestion of lactose in yoghurt in lactose maldigesters when live Lactobacillus delbrueckii subsp. bulgaricus and Streptococcus thermophilus were ingested in yoghurt; the panel concluded that a cause and effect relationship is established, with at least 10^8 CFU live starter microorganisms per gram. In one study about one fifth of the lactase activity contained in yoghurt reached the terminal ileum; in another the effect was destroyed by pasteurisation.
